mainTopic: Which signs prove someone is a כהן (תרומה, חלה, נשיאות כפים), whether they prove יוחסין, and whether תרומה and חלה are דאורייתא today
overview: The גמרא is discussing how a person comes to be treated as a כהן, and whether that status is strong enough to prove his lineage (יוחסין). It first explains the ברייתא's words 'גדולה חזקה' about the כהנים who returned from בבל. One answer is that they moved up from eating תרומה דרבנן to eating תרומה דאורייתא. A second answer is that they still ate only תרומה דרבנן, and the חזקה simply stopped חכמים from making a protective decree. A פסוק in עזרא seems to say they ate תרומה דאורייתא, but the גמרא reads it as forbidding both תרומה and the כהנים' portions of קרבנות. Next, two ברייתות that list נשיאות כפים as proof of כהונה are brought to show it proves lineage. Each time the גמרא pushes the proof off: the listed signs only move a person up from a rabbinic-level gift to a Torah-level one, depending on whether תרומה or חלה is דאורייתא today. This leads to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's report of the רבנן in בי רב saying חלה is דאורייתא. He answers that it is the reverse, and he begins a proof from ״בבואכם״ that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is so great about this presumption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means when it says 'גדולה חזקה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does 'great is presumptive status' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what is special about the חזקה in this story. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהנים just kept doing exactly what they did before, that is an ordinary חזקה and nothing new. So the words 'גדולה חזקה' must be teaching something more, and the גמרא wants to know what.

keyTerms.meaning: Presumptive status: we assume things stay the way they were
'Great is חזקה', the ברייתא's praise of how strong a presumption is
But then / if so

phrases.english: But then, what is the meaning of 'great is presumptive status'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the ברייתא's phrase
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes this חזקה 'great' instead of just ordinary?

steps.title: They moved up from rabbinic תרומה to Torah תרומה
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they ate only תרומה דרבנן. In ארץ ישראל, relying on their חזקה, they ate תרומה דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, in בבל, they ate תרומה that was required only by the רבנן. Now, in ארץ ישראל, they eat תרומה required by the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חזקה was strong enough to move the כהנים up to a more serious level of holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside ארץ ישראל, תרומה is only דרבנן. Once back in ארץ ישראל, the חזקה from eating that lighter תרומה was enough to let them eat תרומה דאורייתא. That upgrade is why the ברייתא calls it 'great'.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה required only by rabbinic law, for example outside ארץ ישראל
תרומה required by Torah law
At first / originally
Now

phrases.english: Originally they ate rabbinic-level תרומה,
phrases.notes: 'Originally' means while they were still in בבל.

phrases.english: now they eat Torah-level תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חזקה let them move up from תרומה דרבנן to תרומה דאורייתא.

steps.title: Second approach: they still ate only rabbinic תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation says they never ate תרומה דאורייתא, and only eating תרומה דאורייתא can prove יוחסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say: even now they ate only rabbinic תרומה and not Torah תרומה. And when we use eating תרומה as proof of lineage, that works only with Torah תרומה, not rabbinic תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to understand the story: the כהנים in ארץ ישראל still ate only תרומה דרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This approach also limits the rule of raising someone from תרומה to יוחסין. Only seeing a person eat תרומה דאורייתא proves he is a real כהן. Seeing him eat תרומה דרבנן proves nothing, so these כהנים were not confirmed for lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you prefer, say: introduces an alternative explanation
We elevate / promote someone to a confirmed status
Lineage, here confirmed status as a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Raising from תרומה to יוחסין means using the fact that someone eats תרומה as proof that he is a real כהן. This approach says that proof works only with תרומה דאורייתא.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
now too, they ate rabbinic-level תרומה,
but Torah-level תרומה they did not eat.
And when we elevate from תרומה to lineage,
it is with Torah-level תרומה;
with rabbinic-level תרומה, we do not elevate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation instead of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reading of the facts plus a limit on the יוחסין rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהנים moved up to תרומה דאורייתא based on their חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They stayed with תרומה דרבנן, which cannot be used to prove יוחסין.

steps.title: Then what is 'great' about the presumption?
steps.stepSummary: Under the second approach, the גמרא again asks what 'גדולה חזקה' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does 'great is presumptive status' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its question, because under the second approach nothing seems to have changed. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהנים ate the same תרומה דרבנן both before and after, the חזקה did nothing new. So the גמרא must find a different meaning for 'great'.

phrases.english: But then, what is the meaning of 'great is presumptive status'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the step 1 question again, now within the second approach
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the חזקה's 'greatness' if they ate only תרומה דרבנן?

steps.title: The חזקה stopped a protective decree
steps.stepSummary: There was a reason to forbid even תרומה דרבנן so they would not come to eat תרומה דאורייתא, but because of the חזקה, חכמים did not make that decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there was reason to make a decree against rabbinic תרומה because of Torah תרומה, we do not make that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the 'greatness' is that the חזקה was strong enough to block a protective decree (גזירה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל, Torah-level תרומה is all around, so there is a real risk that a כהן eating rabbinic תרומה would come to eat Torah תרומה. Normally חכמים might forbid it all as a safeguard. The חזקה was strong enough that they did not.

keyTerms.meaning: To make a protective rabbinic decree (גזירה)
We do not make a decree
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read 'גדולה חזקה'. (1) The חזקה upgraded the כהנים from תרומה דרבנן to תרומה דאורייתא. (2) They ate only תרומה דרבנן, and the חזקה stopped a גזירה against even that.

phrases.english: That even though there is reason to decree
because of Torah-level תרומה,
phrases.notes: The worry is that eating the rabbinic kind could lead them to eat the Torah kind.

phrases.english: we do not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חזקה was strong enough that חכמים did not forbid תרומה דרבנן as a safeguard against eating תרומה דאורייתא.

steps.title: The פסוק in עזרא suggests they did eat Torah תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק forbids only 'קודש הקדשים', which implies they were allowed to eat תרומה דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did they really not eat Torah תרומה? But it is written: 'that they should not eat of the most holy things.' It is only the most holy things they did not eat, which implies they did eat Torah תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second approach, which said they did not eat תרומה דאורייתא, by quoting a פסוק that seems to say they did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids only 'קודש הקדשים', the highest level of holy food. If only that was forbidden, then lower-level holy food like תרומה דאורייתא must have been allowed. That contradicts step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written: introduces a challenge from a פסוק
The most holy things (קרבנות of the highest level)
This implies (an inference from what the text leaves out)

phrases.english: And they did not eat Torah-level תרומה?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כְּתִיב: ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא יֹאכְלוּ מִקֹּדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים״.
phrases.english: But it is written: 'that they should not eat of the most holy things.'
It is of the most holy things that they did not eat;
so Torah-level תרומה they did eat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַתְּרוּמָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא אֲכוּל? וְהָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the returning כהנים did not eat תרומה דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids only קודש הקדשים, which implies that lower holy food, תרומה דאורייתא, was allowed.

steps.title: The פסוק forbids both 'קודש' and 'קדשים'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'קודש הקדשים' as two items: 'קודש', which is תרומה, and 'קדשים', which is the parts of קרבנות given to כהנים. Both were forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: not anything called 'holy' (קודש), as it is written 'no outsider may eat קודש', and not anything called 'holy things' (קדשים), as it is written 'a כהן's daughter married to an outsider may not eat תרומת הקדשים', and the Master said: she may not eat what is set aside from the קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the פסוק's phrase as a list of two separate forbidden foods instead of one category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קודש' is a Torah name for תרומה (ויקרא 22:10). 'קדשים' refers to the parts of קרבנות given to כהנים (ויקרא 22:12). So the פסוק in עזרא forbids both, and that includes תרומה דאורייתא. The second approach stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means: reinterprets a text
A non-כהן (an outsider to כהונה)
What is set aside from קרבנות for the כהנים
The Master said: quotes an earlier teaching

steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'קודש הקדשים' in עזרא is read as two things: 'קודש' (תרומה) and 'קדשים' (the כהנים' portions of קרבנות). So the פסוק does not prove the returning כהנים ate תרומה דאורייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because of this reading, the second approach survives: the returning כהנים ate only תרומה דרבנן, so their eating cannot be used to prove יוחסין.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
not of anything called 'holy',
as it is written: 'And no outsider may eat holy food',
and not of anything called 'holy things',

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבַת כֹּהֵן כִּי תִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ זָר
phrases.english: as it is written: 'And a כהן's daughter, if she is married to an outsider,'
'she shall not eat of the תרומה of the holy things',
and the Master said:
of what is set aside from the holy offerings, she may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the פסוק as listing two separate items
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'קודש הקדשים' is one category, the highest קרבנות, so תרומה was allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'קודש' means תרומה and 'קדשים' means the portions of קרבנות. Both were forbidden, so the כהנים did not eat תרומה דאורייתא.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists נשיאות כפים as proof of being a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that counts נשיאות כפים in בבל as establishing חזקה לכהונה. It suggests this means proof of lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A person is presumed to be a כהן through lifting his hands to bless in בבל, eating חלה in סוריא, and receiving the כהן's gifts in the big cities. The ברייתא lists lifting of hands. Doesn't that mean it proves lineage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to prove that doing נשיאות כפים shows a person is a real כהן by lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names three things that create a חזקה לכהונה, and one of them is נשיאות כפים. The גמרא assumes the חזקה it creates is a חזקה for יוחסין, the strongest kind. That would mean a person who blesses can even be trusted on matters of marriage and family lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as proof
Being presumed to be a כהן
Lifting of hands: the כהנים' blessing
Family lineage: proof that someone is a כהן of pure descent
The gifts given to a כהן from a slaughtered animal

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The presumption of being a כהן is established by
lifting of hands in Babylonia,
and eating חלה in Syria,
and the distribution of gifts in the big cities.
phrases.notes: "Gifts" here means the parts of an animal given to a כהן: the foreleg, the jaw and the stomach.

phrases.english: At any rate, it teaches lifting of hands.
Is it not a proof for lineage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of the people who came back from בבל, the גמרא brings a new source on the same main question.
steps.raayaObject: That נשיאות כפים establishes a חזקה for יוחסין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing נשיאות כפים in בבל as a way to establish חזקה לכהונה.

steps.title: No, it only proves the right to eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: the חזקה from נשיאות כפים may only allow eating תרומה, not prove lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is a proof only for eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by saying the ברייתא's חזקה may be a smaller one, good only for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of חזקה for a כהן. One lets him eat תרומה, and a higher one proves his lineage. The גמרא says the ברייתא can be read as speaking only about the lower level.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce that only כהנים may eat

phrases.english: No, it is for תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the reading of the ברייתא. The ברייתא itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the חזקה was for יוחסין, but it could be only for תרומה.

steps.title: Lifting of hands is listed next to eating חלה, which proves lineage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: נשיאות כפים is listed next to eating חלה. If eating חלה proves lineage, נשיאות כפים should too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches lifting of hands alongside eating חלה! Just as eating חלה proves lineage, lifting of hands should also prove lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection. Items listed together in the same ברייתא should work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumes that eating חלה proves יוחסין. Since the ברייתא lists the items as a matching set, נשיאות כפים should prove יוחסין too. This would bring back the original proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to: listed as a matching case
The portion of dough given to a כהן

phrases.english: But it is taught alongside eating חלה!
Just as eating חלה is a proof for lineage,
so too, lifting of hands is a proof for lineage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נשיאות כפים in the ברייתא only proves the right to eat תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Items in one list should match. Eating חלה is assumed to prove יוחסין, so נשיאות כפים should prove it as well.

steps.title: Eating חלה itself only proves the right to eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that eating חלה also only leads to תרומה. This תנא holds that חלה today is דרבנן and תרומה is דאורייתא, so eating חלה lifts a person up to תרומה, not to יוחסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, eating חלה itself is only a proof for תרומה. This תנא holds that nowadays חלה is a rabbinic law and תרומה is a Torah law. We move a person up from rabbinic חלה to Torah-level תרומה. This follows the way רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע reversed the view of the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the list matching, but turns it around: nothing in the list proves lineage. Every item, eating חלה included, only proves the right to eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed eating חלה proves יוחסין. The answer says no: in this תנא's view חלה today is only דרבנן, so a כהן who eats it can be trusted for the higher, Torah-level תרומה, but not for lineage. This depends on reversing the usual view that חלה is the more serious one, as רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע did.

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays: after the חורבן
A rabbinic law
A Torah law
We raise up: we treat him as a כהן for a higher level
Reversed: flipped the opinions around

steps.confusionAlert: Normally one would think חלה is the more serious one. Here the תנא flips that: חלה is the rabbinic one and תרומה is the Torah one.

phrases.english: No, eating חלה itself is a proof for תרומה.
He holds that nowadays חלה is rabbinic,
and תרומה is from the Torah.
And we raise him up from rabbinic חלה
to Torah-level תרומה.
And this follows the way he reversed them,

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, for the רבנן.
phrases.notes: He flipped the רבנן's opinions around so that חלה is the rabbinic one. The גמרא brings his statement later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the objection's assumption: the matching item also only proves the right to eat תרומה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating חלה proves יוחסין, so נשיאות כפים must prove יוחסין too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating חלה, which is דרבנן today, only lifts a person to Torah-level תרומה. So the list matches, and none of it proves lineage.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: outside ארץ ישראל, lifting of hands counts as proof but threshing-floor shares do not
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says that in ארץ ישראל both נשיאות כפים and receiving a share at the threshing floor establish חזקה לכהונה. In סוריא and wherever the ראש חודש messengers reach, only נשיאות כפים counts as a proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: In ארץ ישראל, a person is presumed to be a כהן through lifting of hands and through the distribution of shares at the threshing floors. In סוריא, and in every place the ראש חודש messengers reach, lifting of hands is a proof, but threshing-floor distribution is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא on the same question. In this ברייתא, נשיאות כפים outside ארץ ישראל is called a real proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside ארץ ישראל, getting תרומה at the threshing floor does not prove anything, but נשיאות כפים still counts as a ראיה. This seems to show that נשיאות כפים was treated more seriously than receiving תרומה. So the source looks like it supports using נשיאות כפים for lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving out תרומה to כהנים at the threshing floors
Messengers sent to tell distant communities which day was ראש חודש
Proof

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The presumption of being a כהן is established by
lifting of hands and distribution at the threshing floors
in ארץ ישראל.
And in Syria, and in every place
that the messengers of ראש חודש reach,
lifting of hands is a proof,
but distribution at the threshing floors is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: חֲזָקָה לִכְהוּנָּה — נְשִׂיאוּת כַּפַּיִם וְחִילּוּק גֳּרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first ברייתא was pushed off, the גמרא brings another source on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That נשיאות כפים carries real proof value, more than receiving תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא distinguishing between ארץ ישראל and the places outside it that the ראש חודש messengers reach.

steps.title: בבל is like סוריא, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds אלכסנדריא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: בבל has the same status as סוריא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says אלכסנדריא of מצרים once did too, because a permanent בית דין sat there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בבל is like סוריא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Also אלכסנדריא of מצרים, in earlier times, because there was a permanent בית דין there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by listing more places where נשיאות כפים counts as a proof, just like in סוריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בבל is added to the places where נשיאות כפים is a proof. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds אלכסנדריא, but only for the past. His reason is the permanent בית דין there, which ties this rule to having a court present.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, the נשיא
In earlier times
A permanent court

steps.whatToRemember: The second ברייתא treats נשיאות כפים as a proof even in places where receiving תרומה proves nothing. In אלכסנדריא, this depended on a permanent בית דין being there.

phrases.english: And Babylonia is like Syria.
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
Also Alexandria of Egypt, in earlier times,
because a permanent court was there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds more places to its rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל has the same status as סוריא. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so did אלכסנדריא in earlier times, because a permanent בית דין was there.

steps.title: The new ברייתא seems to show that lifting hands proves lineage
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists נשיאות כפים as establishing חזקה לכהונה. The גמרא suggests this means full lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches that נשיאות כפים gives a חזקה. Doesn't that mean a חזקה for lineage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the ברייתא from Step 12 and suggests it proves that נשיאות כפים establishes a person's lineage as a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said נשיאות כפים counts as proof even in סוריא. The גמרא assumes 'proof' means full יוחסין, which would let the person marry into pure families.

keyTerms.meaning: in any event; at least
lineage; full proof of pure family descent
the כהנים lifting their hands for ברכת כהנים

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches lifting of hands,
phrases.notes: This refers back to the ברייתא from Step 12, which counted נשיאות כפים as a proof.

phrases.english: is it not for lineage?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת נְשִׂיאוּת כַּפַּיִם, מַאי לָאו לְיוּחֲסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a proof from the ברייתא quoted in Steps 12-13.
steps.raayaObject: That נשיאות כפים establishes חזקה for יוחסין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא listing נשיאות כפים as a proof of כהונה in ארץ ישראל and סוריא.

steps.title: No, it may only be for eating חלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: the חזקה may only allow the person to eat חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the חזקה is only for eating חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. Lifting hands might only let the person eat חלה, not prove his lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are levels of חזקה. A lower level lets someone eat holy food, and a higher level proves lineage. The ברייתא's 'proof' may be the lower level.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of dough given to a כהן

phrases.english: No, for חלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא as proving יוחסין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חזקה may be limited to permission to eat חלה.

steps.title: Lifting hands is listed next to the threshing-floor share
steps.stepSummary: נשיאות כפים is taught alongside חילוק גרנות. Since חילוק גרנות proves lineage, נשיאות כפים should too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches it alongside the sharing of תרומה at the threshing floors. Just as that is for lineage, so too lifting hands is for lineage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The two proofs are taught side by side, so they should mean the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that receiving תרומה at the threshing floor clearly proves יוחסין. Since נשיאות כפים is listed as its parallel, it should also prove יוחסין, not just חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: similar to; parallel with
handing out תרומה to כהנים at the threshing floors

phrases.english: But it is taught parallel to the distribution at the threshing floors:
just as the distribution at the threshing floors is for lineage,
so too lifting of hands is for lineage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the דחיה of Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נשיאות כפים only gives a חזקה for חלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Items listed together share a status, and חילוק גרנות proves יוחסין.

steps.title: The threshing-floor share is also only for חלה
steps.stepSummary: Even חילוק גרנות only lets a person eat חלה. This תנא holds that תרומה today is דרבנן and חלה is דאורייתא, so a person is moved up from rabbinic תרומה to Torah-level חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the threshing-floor share itself is only for חלה. This תנא holds that תרומה today is rabbinic and חלה is from the Torah. We move a person up from rabbinic תרומה to Torah-level חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by lowering both proofs. Neither one proves lineage; both only allow eating חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting rabbinic תרומה shows you eat something holy only by rabbinic law. That lets us trust you with the higher Torah-level חלה, but not with full יוחסין. The parallel still holds, just at a lower level.

keyTerms.meaning: itself
he holds; this is his view
in our time, after the חורבן
we raise up; we promote

steps.confusionAlert: Here תרומה is the LOWER level and חלה the HIGHER one, because this תנא holds that תרומה today is only דרבנן. Don't assume תרומה is always the more serious of the two.

phrases.english: No, the distribution at the threshing floors itself is for חלה.
He holds that תרומה nowadays is rabbinic,
and חלה is from the Torah.
And we raise up from rabbinic תרומה
to Torah-level חלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets both parallel items at a lower level.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חילוק גרנות proves יוחסין, so נשיאות כפים must too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both only raise a person from rabbinic תרומה to Torah-level חלה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer depends on how serious תרומה and חלה are today, which opens the discussion that follows.

steps.title: The רבנן in בי רב: חלה today is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע reports that the רבנן in בי רב said that even if תרומה today is דרבנן, חלה is דאורייתא. Their proof: during the fourteen years of conquest and division, Israel was obligated in חלה but not in תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב הונא son of רב יהושע found the רבנן saying. He said: I found the רבנן in the study hall of רב sitting and saying: Even according to the one who says תרומה today is rabbinic, חלה is from the Torah. For during the seven years they conquered and the seven years they divided the land, they were obligated in חלה but not in תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the view in Step 17, that חלה is more serious than תרומה today. It does this through a report by רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חלה obligation started as soon as Israel entered the land. תרומה only started after the land was conquered and divided. So חלה does not depend on the same conditions as תרומה, and it can stay דאורייתא even when תרומה is only דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: I found them
the study hall of רב
the seven years of conquering and seven years of dividing ארץ ישראל under יהושע

phrases.aramaic: וְכִדְאַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: And it is like when רב הונא son of רב יהושע found the Sages.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: For רב הונא son of רב יהושע said:
I found the Sages in the study hall of רב,
sitting and saying:
Even according to the one who says
that תרומה nowadays is rabbinic,
חלה is from the Torah.
For during the seven years that they conquered and the seven that they divided —
phrases.notes: This means the first fourteen years after entering the land under יהושע.

phrases.english: they were obligated in חלה, and not obligated in תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִדְאַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and expands the premise of Step 17, that חלה is דאורייתא while תרומה is דרבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if תרומה today is דרבנן, חלה is דאורייתא, since חלה applied before תרומה did.

steps.title: רב הונא argues the reverse: חלה today is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע told them: On the contrary, even if תרומה today is דאורייתא, חלה is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to them: On the contrary! Even according to the one who says תרומה today is from the Torah, חלה is rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back against the רבנן and claims the exact opposite. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said חלה is the stronger obligation today. רב הונא says חלה is the weaker one. In his view, even someone who holds תרומה is still דאורייתא would agree that חלה is only דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: on the contrary; the reverse is true
I said to them

phrases.english: And I said to them:
On the contrary, even according to the one who says
that תרומה nowadays is from the Torah —
חלה is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly opposes the view of the רבנן in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's claim that חלה today is דאורייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reverses the claim: חלה is weaker than תרומה, so it is דרבנן even if תרומה is דאורייתא.

steps.title: Proof from ״בבואכם״: חלה needs all of Israel in the land
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״בבואכם״ that the Torah obligation of חלה depends on the coming of all of Israel, not some of them. The גמרא begins to apply this to the return under עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'When you come into the land.' If it says 'when you come,' I might think the obligation began once two or three spies entered. So the פסוק says 'when you come': I meant the coming of all of you, not the coming of some of you. And when עזרא brought them up...
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא backs up his claim with a ברייתא. The obligation of חלה depends on all of Israel being in the land. The sentence about עזרא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word ״בבואכם״ means all of you together. Under עזרא only part of the people returned, so the Torah obligation of חלה would not apply in the בית שני era and after. That would make חלה today only דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: when you (all) come
spies
the פסוק teaches
some of you

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'When you come into the land.'
If it says 'when you come,'

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל מִשֶּׁנִּכְנְסוּ לָהּ שְׁנַיִם וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְרַגְּלִים —
phrases.english: I might think from when two or three spies entered it —
the פסוק says: 'When you come.'
phrases.notes: The same word is read again, now stressing the plural 'you all'.

phrases.english: I said it with the coming of all of you,
and not with the coming of some of you.
And when עזרא brought them up,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רב הונא's claim in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That חלה today is only דרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ״בבואכם״ to mean that the obligation applies only when all of Israel is in the land.
